clues: A volcanic archipelago straddling the equator, roughly 900 km west of the South American mainland.
A young naturalist arrived here aboard HMS Beagle on 15 September 1835, and what he saw later shaped a famous theory.

reveal.explanation: The Galápagos Islands are located around the equator, 898 km west of the mainland of South America; islands in the chain lie in both hemispheres. HMS Beagle, with Charles Darwin aboard, reached the archipelago on 15 September 1835.

sources.excerpt: The Galápagos Islands (0.500°S 90.500°W) are located around the equator, 485 nautical miles (898 km) west of the mainland of South America. Straddling the equator, islands in the chain are located in both the Northern and Southern hemispheres. HMS Beagle reached the Galápagos on 15 September 1835 with the young naturalist Charles Darwin aboard.
